title: the five Lows of the review of #1478 (H-133's key operations)

findings.claim: 1478-1: seven unit tests ran rotate-kek against the host's real /etc/credstore.encrypted (stat, and as root flock and decrypt); fixed: an autouse unit fixture puts the credential's place under the test root

1478-2: rotate-kek --backend file by an account that cannot look in the credential's folder went on and said done, the credential left on the old KEK; fixed: refused before any change unless --no-tpm, which is refused beside --seal-tpm, where a credential is there and with another back end
1478-3: the exact 0644 and 0600 mode pin of the H-111 re-run test ran only as root, so never in CI; fixed: it runs on every run and asks audit_sign.pub to be there

1478-4: as an ordinary user the owner record was keyed by inode and never forgot one, so a folder made again read as the services' with no chown and two hand-over mutants passed; fixed: a freed inode forgets its owner

1478-5: the no-tool-check mutant survived (H-133 said 13 of 13 caught) and the 669/667 counts named no file list; fixed: a --seal-tpm new-board test with no tool, and this page names the files and the command
